PICK A TAPE. PLAY THE BAD GUY.

No Survivors is an isometric action roguelite built around a growing collection of VHS horror and action movies. You play the villain. Hunt people who run from you, build an increasingly ridiculous arsenal, and fight back when the authorities arrive.

NEW TAPE. NEW NIGHTMARE.

Each tape brings a different villain, setting, arsenal, objectives and story. A masked slasher loose in the woods. A killer machine hunting through city streets. More villains and movie-inspired worlds are planned as the collection grows.

Here are the first examples from the shelf:
  • Camp Crestwood — playable in the free demo. Put on the Butcher's mask and hunt campers through cabins and woods. Collect souls and face an escalating police and military response, armed with machetes, shotguns, chainsaws, attack dogs and a few much worse ideas.
  • Judgment Thursday — in development for the full game. Become a killer machine in Los Angeles, 1989. Track ten marked targets through streets and shops, scan identities and follow address leads. A morphing blade, firearms, explosives and drones help you reach the protector guarding your final target.

BUILD YOUR OWN KIND OF MONSTER

Collect XP, choose upgrades, and combine weapons with passives and evolutions. Each tape has its own arsenal to experiment with. Find combinations that turn a hunt into a massacre, then try a different build on the next run.

HIT IT. LAUNCH IT. BLOW IT UP.

Break through walls, smash props, launch enemies and trigger explosive chain reactions. Cabins, shops, trees and vehicles become part of the fight as your weapons tear through the surroundings.

PANIC ON THE RADIO

People panic, police call for backup, and the situation gets increasingly ridiculous. Tape-specific dialogue, radio exchanges, dark humour and movie references follow the chaos, with cinematic endings shaped by how your hunt plays out.

Start with Camp Crestwood in the free demo. Wishlist No Survivors for the full collection.

The game replaces traditional cards with 'equipment + actions' and card cycling with action cooldowns. A limited battlefield adds depth to combat decisions, the rune system opens far more room for customizing equipment, and equipment upgrades provide numerical growth for your build. Over a hundred enemies offer varied challenges. Three completely different playable characters are available, each with content unlocked as you progress. Two additional difficulties are also included, each with its own new system that raises the challenge while offering more build options.

Equipment + Actions

You can hold up to nine pieces of equipment in a run. Each piece has one passive effect, up to three actions, and several rune effects. During combat, actions are drawn by equipment: all actions on a piece are drawn into your hand together. Equipment can only be purchased from the shop.

 

Action Cooldowns

There is no discard pile; instead, actions go on cooldown. After an action is used, it must wait a number of turns before it can be used again.

 

A Limited Battlefield

The field holds multiple characters who can move left and right. Every piece of equipment has its own attack range, and its actions inherit that range. Enemy attacks also have ranges, so you can dodge by moving - but be careful not to be cornered.

Runes and Upgrades

After each battle you receive rewards such as healing, money, actions, and runes - your main source of actions and runes. They can also be bought in the shop. Upgrading applies to equipment: an upgrade strengthens both the equipment's effect and its actions. Runes cannot be upgraded.

 

A Wide Variety of Enemies

A run consists of fifteen battles. In each you must withstand attacks from several enemies; kills earn money. Every fifth battle is a boss fight. Every enemy has unique intents and abilities, and boss enemies wield powerful, deadly powers.

Multiple Playable Characters

The game currently has three playable characters. The Knight defeats enemies with basic attacks and defense. The Sorcerer wields water, ice, fire, lightning, and wind. The Summoner fights through summoned minions. Only the Knight is available at first; the others unlock through play.

Advanced Difficulties

Two additional difficulties are available. Clearing one unlocks the next, and each step strengthens enemies. The first advanced difficulty enables the blessing system: after defeating a boss, choose one of three blessings - their effects are very powerful. The second enables the optional difficulty system: at the start of each new battle, choose one of three modifiers. Each offers both risk and reward, and you may take or skip them as needed.

At least one person in this lobby is a Killer... Nobody saw it happen... It's your job to work it out and make sure they meet their maker. A comedic multiplayer where reading the room matters just as much as aiming and where a perfectly tense standoff can be ruined (improved?) by everyone suddenly shrinking to the size of a soda can...

  • Play online or with your friends, up to 16 players (4 / 8 / 12 / 16 supported)

  • 16 maps out of the box

    • Steam Workshop support to make your own or use the community made maps!

  • Play with your friends, or total strangers - friends-only lobbies, a full server browser and dedicated server support

Bystander

Survive, and don't get blamed. Anyone can identify a corpse - but can you provde who did it before someone points the finger at you? Scour the environment for random gifts, cash money or just weapons to defend yourself with. And remember, at every turn, those who you trust the most, might just turn out to betray you. 

Detective (4+ Players)

In bigger lobbies you will be the ultimate assistant, use your specialised skillset to aid the Bystanders and clutch the victory. Purchase effective tools from the shop to aid you in your mission, but be careful, everyone knows your role. Killers will be out to slaughter you at the first opportunity and Bystanders will trust your every word, so be careful who you blame.

Killer

Act natural and don't raise suspicion. Remember, witnesses can talk and bodies leave evidence. Your goal is to eliminate every non-Killer player in the lobby to earn the ultimate bragging rights within your circle, but don't get too cocky, you might just fall into a trap. Purchase specalised weaponry and equipment from the shop but there's a catch. Don't let anyone see you with them, or you'll be scrambling for an excuse - or the trigger. The choice is yours.

Your Decisions Matter

Whether you play as a Bystander, a Detective or a Killer, your decisions affect your reputation with your friends. Over time they'll learn who can be trusted and who is a trigger-happy know-it-all. Make the wrong choices and your reputation will dwindle, let it fall too far and you'll meet your demise, potentially ending your winning-streak!

Pure Chaos, Every Round

This is a comedy first and a whodunnit second. Mystery gifts, phone-box killer contracts and pure chaos events sling 22 different effects across the lobby at the worst possible moments, including:

  • Moon gravity firefights and "Honey, I shrunk the kids" brawls

  • Giant heads, clown hats, bouncy legs and banana-slick floors

  • Disco guns that make you dance, confetti guns that do nothing, reverse cards that fling your bad luck onto someone else

  • "The floor is lava" - a childhood classic brought to life, jump or feel the heat of the ground

Answer the phone. Or don't.

A mysterious phonebox starts ringing. If you're the Killer, it's a timed contract with a reward for a specific mark. If you're not the Killer and you pick it up anyway you get one warning to not be so nosey... Just remember the phrase "Curiosity killed the cat"...

Gear Up

Find stacks of cash around the map and spend it at the in-round shop: deploy a decoy, disguise yourself as another player, revive a teammate with a defib, throw off your opponent with carefully placed speakers or torch the evidence with a molotov. Weapons live in the world - locate them, pick them up and if things go really wrong, throw them somewhere nobody will ever find them...

Make it yours

  • Proximity voice chat - hear people scheme, panic, and lie in real time (and yes, there's a gag that mutes you)

  • Character customisation - skin tones and wardrobe to make the character truly one of a kind

  • Emotes - Taunt, cheer, or dance. Either in the battlefield, or on the body of your enemy.

Darkness is not your enemy. This time, it is your shelter.

Stay quiet.

Brendyk Wos returns to the village where he grew up after the death of his parents, but finds a community that seems to exist beneath a sickly calm. The locals are still there, working, praying, and surviving under the influence of a company that long ago ceased to be merely an economic presence.

The priest has vanished. The new town lies in ruins. And no one seems willing to speak about what was lost when the earth began to give way. What kind of faith remains in a place ruled by fear? What secrets still breathe beneath the rubble?

Step into what remains of the new town: an urban expansion built on the promise of work, order, and a future, now reduced to ruins. Scour shattered streets, abandoned buildings, maintenance tunnels, and industrial facilities as you gather clues about the missing and the secrets the company has kept hidden.

Every area demands attention. Locked doors, forgotten documents, distant sounds, and traces left behind can reveal new paths — or warn you that something is drawing near. In Nobody's Erde, to explore is not merely to advance: it is to decide when to investigate, when to hide, and when to flee.

  • Explore a decaying Eastern European village, still inhabited yet controlled by the influence of a powerful company.

  • Scour the new town, a devastated urban expansion marked by abandoned industrial facilities.

  • Investigate documents, traces, and environmental details to uncover what happened to the priest, the locals, and the region.

  • Survive encounters with strange creatures that have made the rubble their hunting ground.

  • Advance with caution: listening, observing, hiding, and fleeing can be as important as finding the next path.

  • Dive into an atmosphere of religious horror, industrial conspiracy, and cosmic terror.

Uncover a story of corrupted faith, human ambition, and horrors buried beneath the promise of progress. As Brendyk moves between the village and the ruins of the new town, every clue reveals a deeper layer of a tragedy no one seems willing to face.

In Nobody's Erde, surviving is only the beginning; understanding the truth may be the real danger.

Non-Sense is a cute-dark 2D narrative adventure RPG about helping Fran rebuild what’s missing—by pushing through surreal nightmares and bringing that hard-won clarity back into everyday life.

By day, you’ll explore familiar places and routines—work, the plaza, therapy, classes, commutes—choosing what to engage with, what to say, and what to focus on. By night, you’ll step into a shifting dream world guided by Moorsh, facing Shadows in tense shooter-style encounters and puzzle-like challenges. Each victory restores a piece of Fran’s perception, opening new interactions, details, and opportunities in the waking world.

Progress isn’t just measured in fights won or paths unlocked, but in the quiet returns: noticing what used to slip by, reconnecting with ordinary moments, and finding the strength to keep showing up.

Key Features

  • Narrative-driven adventure RPG / visual novel blend built around exploration and dialogue choices

  • Two intertwined worlds: grounded daily life and a surreal dream realm with rising intensity

  • Perception-based progression: recover what’s missing in dreams, then use it to reveal new details and unlock new interactions in everyday scenes

  • Puzzles and side activities rooted in ordinary life (including creative and practical tasks)

  • Dream encounters with shooter-style combat mixed with riddle-like beats and story moments

If you’re drawn to story-rich adventures that mix the familiar with the surreal, add Non-Sense to your wishlist—and follow Fran’s journey as the dream world closes in and everyday life starts to change.

RoRoKaii's magnum opus, renowned across the entire RoRoKaii Discord: an incremental game unlike anything you've ever seen.

Design Your Own Transport Network

Lay lines between procedurally generated archipelagos to connect different types of nodes.

The gameplay is simple:

  • Place nodes

  • Then connect them

Simple is possible, but simple is unlikely: you'll need to leverage island shapes, relic effects, and legendary character abilities to build your node empire:

Shorter paths? Or more merges?

I don't know.

Expand Your Automated Empire

Unlock increasingly advanced nodes.

Research various upgrades and discover synergies between different nodes.

Continuously optimize your layout to keep your network growing — transport won't stop even when you're away.

Every Island Is a New Challenge

Each run generates a brand new archipelago map.

Different island biomes offer unique bonuses. Reset islands to gain new power-ups, and use relics and legendary characters to forge different development paths.

Relax and Watch the Network Run

No frantic clicking, no stressful countdowns!

Just watch thousands of tokens race through your network, converging and merging into an endless stream of revenue!

Game Features

  • Truly relaxed idle gameplay

  • Procedurally generated archipelago maps — a different layout every run

  • Multiple nodes, upgrades, and synergies waiting to be discovered

  • Island reset, permanent progression, relic and legendary character systems

  • Continuously optimize your network for higher efficiency and greater returns

The game has 5 node types — doesn't sound like much. But combined with relics, legendary characters, and various upgrades, it's more than enough to build complex networks. Math, kid. Do some math!

So it must be a deeply strategic game, right?

Answer: it's debatable.

This minimalist game is also steeped in zen aesthetics, with a soundtrack that reacts to your network!

In short: this is an incremental game like nothing you've ever played!

Nordic is a PS1-aesthetic "foddylike" cross-country skiing game with drop-in drop-out multiplayer.  Nordic captures what makes cross-country skiing great; rhythm & cadence, the calm of nature and exploring the natural world with your friends!  It also captures the gruelling nature of the sport.  You must manage your energy and time your moments to push - especially if you want to be competitive and race.  All of this with complete control of each of your limbs.  

Game Design

Nordic skiing is not alpine.  Don't expect to see crazy flips or other SSX-style tricks.  Nordic is about rhythm and pace.  It's about finding your groove (sometimes literally, in classic ski tracks).  I always thought nordic skiing would translate well to a video game if it could capture the tactile feel of the technique on a game controller.  For that reason, the game has been designed with a controller in mind.  I have given a "foddylike" approach to the control scheme as you have skill expression over each of your limbs.  In this way you are free to ski in whatever style you want. 

Features

  • Skate and classic technique

  • Independent controls for each limb - ski for real, and use actual classic skiing techniques 

  • Ski Glide that rewards proper cadence

  • Energy — legs and arms tire and contribute to energy consumption, managing this is key to effective skiing

Game Modes

  • Nordic Valley — a crafted resort with that serves as a social hub and features races and capture the flag

  • Endless Trail — a procedural winter valley with an infinite groomed track through the pines

  • Race Mode — race a pre-defined track online or against bots

  • Custom Trail — ski real GPS trails from around the world, with true elevation, difficulty signs, and a paper trail map

Winter Atmosphere

  • Day and night cycles

  • Weather simulation

  • Wandering animals

  • PSX aesthetic

If it looks like a duck, floats like a duck and squeaks like a duck... check again.

1998. Night shift, Line 3, Puddleworth Rubber Co. Your job is quality control: every rubber duck that comes down the belt gets inspected, and every duck gets a verdict. SHIP or REJECT.

Most of them are just ducks.

Inspect

  • Pick units up and turn them over. Squeeze them: a real duck squeaks.
  • Float-test them in the tank: a real duck floats upright.
  • Check the factory stamp under UV light, weigh them on the bench scale, and follow a rulebook that grows every night.
  • Shred the defects. Ship the rest. Try not to think about where the rejects go.

Put them away

Shipped units don't just disappear. Carry the tote out into the warehouse, scan each duck and shelve it in the right aisle, bay and level, while the motion-sensor lights stutter on above you one aisle at a time.

Don't look away

Some units breathe when you squeeze them. Some sink, and turn to face you from the bottom of the tank. Some move when you're not looking, and the stock on the shelves has started doing it too. Something is knocking on the exit door. And something at the far end of the warehouse is much, much bigger than a duck.

Features

  • A first-person horror sorting game with a lo-fi PS1 look: vertex wobble, dithering and CRT scanlines
  • Night after night of new rules, new anomalies and new ways for the warehouse to go wrong
  • Company perks: spend your wages on a UV lamp, a bench scale, a better scanner, coffee and more
  • Blackouts, radio glitches, knocking, and things right behind you
  • Captions that describe every important sound

Headphones recommended.

Notoris 2 is a 2.5D single-player grand strategy game inspired by Romance of the Three Kingdoms, where legendary officers forge rivalries and alliances in an open ended sandbox shaped by your choices and turn based battles.

You don't have to be the ruler. Experience classic grand strategy through the eyes of a single officer, rising from a lowly lieutenant to trusted administrator and beyond. Earn influence through cunning proposals and battlefield valor, and carve your own path to power.

✦ Start as a lowly officer, not a king

✦ Take on civil assignments to build your reputation

✦ Rise through the ranks, or scheme your way to independence

✦ Every officer you meet has their own stats, traits, ambitions and grudges

Gold buys armies. Influence buys people.
Your officers aren't puppets, they're ambitious individuals with their own goals. The Influence System gives you control over how much autonomy your subordinates have. Spend it wisely at critical moments, like taking control of an allied army or pushing a proposal through the faction council. Find the sweet spot between control and chaos.

Influence isn't just flavor. It's a core mechanic that solves an age-old strategy game problem: giving players meaningful agency without turning the AI into mindless puppets.



✦ Submit proposals to shape your faction's destiny

✦ Spend influence to push your plans, or block a rival's

✦ Win the vote, and your plan becomes your lord's command





✦ Forge alliances, rivalries, and betrayals with hundreds of unique officers

✦ Navigate a web of influence where even your subordinates pursue their own ambitions

✦ Recruit enemy officers, or lose your own to a better offer




✦ Deploy armies on grid-based battlefields where terrain and positioning decide victory

✦ Execute devastating officer abilities that can turn the tide of war

✦ Siege cities, spread control, and outmaneuver your enemies

✦ Every battle matters. Lose your best generals as captives and feel the consequences



✦ Transform from loyal retainer to rebel warlord to emperor

✦ Manage cities, assign officers, and balance the needs of your growing realm

✦ Watch the campaign map evolve as others rise and fall around you





Escape the constraints of strict history and enter a world where:

✦ Dark fantasy aesthetics meet the political intrigue of the Three Kingdoms era

✦ History's iconic rivalries and betrayals reemerge as timeless character arcs

✦ A new era of possibility where interpersonal dramas play out in unexpected ways, shaped by your hand





This is a passion project from a solo developer who grew up on Three Kingdoms games, supported by a small team of part time contractors who share the vision.

I'm attempting to bring together the best features from across the history of Three Kingdoms games: the deep officer roleplay that blended RPG into grand strategy like nothing before or since, and the tactical grid combat that always felt so close to greatness but never quite reached it. By fusing these elements and many others together, I'm hoping to create the definitive experience fans have been waiting decades for. Your support means everything to a tiny indie project attempting to punch above its weight class.

Introduction

What if increasing your character's max health didn't just keep you alive, but also accelerated your ability to cast high-powered spells? In the game design architecture of Nozile, traditional combat rules are reframed through an interconnected resource-cycling engine where survivability, tactical stances, and skill usage continuously feed into one another.

In this lesson, you will learn to:

  • Analyze the resource-cycling loop of MP consumption and recovery in Nozile.

  • Differentiate between the three core weapon styles and their tactical loadout synergies.

  • Evaluate how player parameters—Health, Intelligence, and Dexterity—synergize to drive combat performance.

The Engine of Combat: Resource Cycling and MP Regeneration

At its core, Nozile is structured around a resource-cycling system where combat tempo is dictated by how efficiently players spend and recover Magic Points (MP). Active combat skills consume MP upon use, preventing endless skill spamming and forcing players to stay mindful of their resource reserves.

To keep action dynamic rather than static, Nozile provides two primary channels for regaining MP:

  • Passive Skill Triggers: Players recover MP actively by fulfilling specific tactical conditions during battle, which trigger recovery-focused passive skills.

  • Parameter-Driven Auto-Recovery: MP automatically regenerates over time, but the speed of this regeneration is tied directly to the player's Health parameter.

Imagine a baseline auto-recovery rate set at 1 MP per second. By investing in your character's Health parameter, the game engine accelerates this recovery tick rate—either by reducing the frame delay between recovery pulses or increasing the amount of MP restored with each pulse. Increasing your defensive durability directly boosts your engine's magic output.

Tactical Stances: Weapon Styles and Loadout Choice

Combat options in Nozile are built on a foundation of 6 distinct weapon types. While weapons vary in form, all weapons share 3 standardized combat styles. Before stepping into battle, players must choose exactly 2 styles to bring into their active loadout.

Each style fulfills a distinct tactical role in managing power output and resource replenishment:

  • Offense Style: Focused purely on high offensive power. However, it contains zero passive skills for MP recovery, serving exclusively as a resource burner to deal heavy damage.

  • Defense Style: Features lower individual skill damage, but compensates with wide area-of-effect (AoE) attacks. Most importantly, it is equipped with specialized passive skills dedicated to recovering MP, functioning as your battle battery.

  • Balance Style: Offers a middle ground between Offense and Defense, balancing damage output, range, and resource maintenance.

Equipping a dual loadout—such as pairing Defense with Offense—allows players to create a complementary rhythm. You can unleash AoE attacks in the Defense style to harvest MP through passive triggers, then swap to the Offense style to dump that accumulated energy into devastating burst attacks.

Parameter Synergy: Building Your Character

Character customization in Nozile centers on core parameters that modify both basic stats and underlying skill effectiveness. Understanding how these parameters interact allows players to craft tailored playstyles.

The key player parameters include:

  • Health (体力): Expands your maximum Hit Points (HP) and directly accelerates the baseline tick rate of automatic MP recovery.

  • Intelligence (知力): Acts as a multiplicative force multiplier. It enhances the numerical effectiveness of attack skills, magic skills, and passive skills by a fixed scaling factor. Higher Intelligence makes both active damage spells and passive MP restoration significantly more potent.

  • Dexterity (器用度): Increases combat precision by elevating your Critical Rate, boosting overall damage consistency.

Because Intelligence scales passive skill effects multiplicatively while Health speeds up base auto-recovery timers, players can create distinct builds—such as high-Health frontline regenerators or high-Intelligence glass-cannon spellcasters.

Summary

Mastering Nozile requires treating combat mechanics as an interconnected engine where resource expenditure, weapon stance swapping, and character attributes work in tandem to maintain constant battle momentum.

Key Takeaways:

  • Resource Cycling: Spells consume MP, which is replenished via conditional passive skill triggers and automated recovery.

  • Health-Driven Regeneration: Investing in Health raises maximum HP while speeding up baseline MP auto-recovery timers.

  • Dual-Style Loadouts: Players choose 2 of 3 standardized styles (Offense, Defense, Balance) across 6 weapon types to balance damage dealing with MP generation.

  • Multiplicative Parameter Scaling: Intelligence boosts the strength of attacks, magic, and passive skills multiplicatively, while Dexterity increases Critical Rate.

Weapon Styles and the Sword & Shield

Every combatant in Nozile has access to 6 distinct weapon types. While weapons offer varied combat feels, every single weapon relies on three universal combat styles: Offense, Defense, and Balance. When heading into battle, players select exactly two of these styles to equip simultaneously, blending their distinct skills and passives.

  • Offense Style: Focused purely on raw damage output. It features high-potency single-target skills, but carries zero passive skills for MP recovery. You must spend MP aggressively while relying on your secondary style or stat auto-recovery to gain it back.

  • Defense Style: Features wide-area control skills with lower base damage, paired with passives heavily specialized in harvesting MP back during combat.

  • Balance Style: Offers a middle ground with versatile survival utility, damage-amplifying fields, and conditional recovery passives.

To see this synergy in action, look at the foundational benchmark weapon: the One-Handed Sword & Shield. Straightforward and predictable, it relies on no complex unique resources, making it the perfect vehicle for mastering style rotation:

  • Offense Loadout: Packs Continuous Thrust (1,500 MP), a tight 10-hit strike that melts single targets, and Combo Amplification (a toggle skill raising damage up to +60%). Its passives boost critical hit rate as your combo counts climb and increase attack power as your MP drops low.

  • Defense Loadout: Features Crescent Slash (1,800 MP), a 180° front sweep for crowd pushback, alongside Guardian Domain, a stationary zone providing 40% damage reduction and massive enemy slow. Crucially, its passives recover MP when your red health gauge restores or whenever normal attacks land.

  • Balance Loadout: Delivers Shield Charge (2,000 MP) with full invulnerability during the charge, and Battle Domain, which buffs outgoing damage by +50% while continuously chipping away at enemy health. Its passives restore MP on successful guards and boost attack speed at low MP.

For first-time adventurers, the game fixes your initial setup to Offense × Defense. Why? Because the Defense style restores MP simply by landing basic attacks. Even if a novice player hasn't mastered guard timings or domain placement, hitting enemies automatically cycles their MP pool, keeping the combat engine running smoothly!

And when that life comes to an end, another one will begin.

With millions of possible combinations of choices, encounters, relationships, and events shaping your existence, no two playthroughs will ever tell the same story.

You won’t simply play Oda’s life.

You’ll discover who Oda could have become.

• 1 year = 1 event: each year of your life, a new event is presented to you.

• 2 choices per event: decide how Oda reacts and shape the course of his life.

• Long-term consequences: your decisions can influence the events, relationships, and opportunities that appear years later.

• Millions of possibilities: choices, encounters, relationships, and events can combine in countless ways to create a different life every time you play.

• Reincarnation: when Oda dies, choose to begin an entirely new life or relive the exact same life to try to change certain events and alter his fate.

• Every life is unique: no two playthroughs will unfold exactly the same way.

Hundreds of cats. One very busy island.

Build a home for a whole lot of cats, then let them get to work.

Odd Eggs is a cozy automation and management sim about turning a small island into a thriving community. Plan your buildings, set up production chains, and recruit residents to lead your furry workforce. The cats handle their daily routines while you decide what to build next. Settle in on your own, or visit friends online to sell produce together and lend a paw with construction.

Start small. Get things humming.

Assign workers, arrange your buildings, and keep the goods moving. Your cats carry supplies and get on with their jobs, leaving you to shape the bigger picture. Start with a few simple resources and build up to a busy production network, one manageable step at a time.

From a tent to a bustling town

Chop wood, haul stone, process beets, and put those resources to work. Unlock new goods, technologies, and building upgrades as your island grows. There is something satisfying about looking back at a thriving settlement and remembering when it was just a tent.

A workforce with a life of its own

Even hardworking cats need a break. Watch them line up for work, stop for a meal, and gather around after hours. Some may find time to slack off, too. Keep an eye on production, or take a moment to enjoy the little routines that make your island feel alive.

Get to know your residents

Meet dozens of residents with their own personalities, abilities, and stories. Assign them to lead different jobs, collect outfits to make each look your own, and get to know them through dreams and everyday events.

Explore new biomes

Take your growing community beyond its first island, from sandy deserts to snowy landscapes. Each biome brings different resources and building challenges, giving you new ways to expand and rethink your production chains.

Make a little time for yourself

Put down the building plans and pick up a fishing rod. Grow flowers, breed new colors, and try your hand at cooking. Between bigger projects, there is always room for a quiet afternoon and a new recipe.

Lend a friend a paw

Visit friends' islands online, sell produce together, and help with construction. Whether you are tending your own town or pitching in on a friend's next project, there is plenty to keep your paws busy.

A note from Mobi Studio

We are a three-person indie team from Shanghai, China. We love automation games, cats, and the small details that make a game world feel lived in. With Odd Eggs, we wanted to bring those things together: growing production chains, a home to make your own, and tiny workers with busy lives. We would love to hear your ideas and see how your island grows. Come share your stories in the Steam discussions.

HOW DEEP WILL YOU DIG?

A strange mountain sits in Your uncle's backyard and you're determined to find out what's hiding inside. Dig through layers of earth and rock, discover valuable resources, sell your finds, and use the money to upgrade your equipment.

The deeper you go, the stranger things become.

Odd Stories: Backyard Mountain is an exploration adventure game in which what seems to be an ordinary favor for your uncle turns into the discovery of a mystery hidden deep underground.

Your uncle has gone on a business trip, leaving you the keys to his newly built house. However, there is one problem—a huge mountain of dirt and rocks behind the house that he hasn't had time to remove yet. What initially seems like nothing more than an ordinary pile of rubble soon turns out to hide something far more mysterious. How deep will you dare to dig?

Put on your exoskeleton and begin the excavation. Mine minerals, sell them, invest the money you earn in upgrades, and gradually increase your machine's capabilities. Dig faster, move more efficiently, and reach deeper and deeper, uncovering the secrets hidden beneath the surface.

Each new layer of the mountain brings new resources and even more questions. What is really beneath your uncle's house? Why is this mountain here in the first place? The answers await those who are not afraid to dig deep enough.

Key Features

  • Dig through a huge mountain and discover its underground layers.

  • Mine a variety of minerals and sell them to earn money.

  • Purchase upgrades that increase your digging speed and your exoskeleton's movement speed.

  • Discover mysterious objects and secrets hidden deep underground.

  • Upgrade your equipment to reach places that were previously inaccessible.

The deeper you dig, the more you realize that this mountain is not just an ordinary pile of dirt.

WHAT’S NEXT

A free update lands in December with Endless mode past Floor 100, new relics and a new minion, plus French, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese, Korean and Traditional Chinese.

More on the roadmap after that.

Roll five dice. Hold what you like, reroll the rest, and chase a poker hand. Every hand becomes an army, and your minions fight on their own.

"Balatro meets autobattler" - AboboKnows

EVERY ARMY STARTS WITH A ROLL

Each die carries a minion. Roll high and more of them show up. Hold a promising pair, gamble on a straight, or chase the full house that brings the whole crew in.

Unused dice can burst into Gold, XP, healing, extra damage or another minion. Even a low roll can help.

WATCH THE DICE COME ALIVE

Tanks take the front, ranged minions fire from behind them, and healers keep the crew standing. Pick your recruits, commit your hand, then watch both armies go at it. Now and then, an enemy even has the nerve to heckle your roll.

COME BACK SWINGING

Some fights post a bounty: roll the dice it asks for, and one of the prizes is a Second Wave. Once the battle starts, you get a fresh hand with two rolls to send in another army. If your first army falls, the surviving enemies wait for you.

RECRUIT. COLLECT. DEPLOY.

Unspent Gold is yours to keep when a run ends. Buy new recruits, strengthen future armies with permanent shop upgrades, and upgrade the Backpack for your deeper starts.

Build your collection and chase 100 Steam achievements.

TEMPT FATE BETWEEN BATTLES

Between fights, memorize a disappearing roll, stop the reels at just the right moment, or try your luck at a dice table. A lucky stop can change the run.

OPEN IT AND SEE

Chests along the way let you pick a prize. A sealed goblin envelope is a 50/50: 150 Gold or a level. Opening Salvo makes every minion's first hit deal 50% more damage for the rest of the run.

REST. SHOP. REBUILD.

Camps let you heal, change your recruits or carve an unwanted face off a die. Shop with a shady goblin and collect relics that bend the rules, each with a boon and a catch.

Every 20 floors you reach a checkpoint: keep going, or cash out to bank your Gold and end the run. Each checkpoint also unlocks a deeper starting floor. Ride the lift down to a welcome camp, where the bard tosses you a Backpack of upgrades and offers one free pick, such as a relic.

DESCEND AS FAR AS YOU DARE

100 floors. Ten zones, each with a boss who rolls dice of their own. New enemies, stranger stops and tougher fights keep turning up as you go down.

The full game launches November 16, 2026. Wishlist it so you don't miss it, or try the free demo first. The demo is separate: no saves, progress or achievements carry over to the full game.

About Offside Deal

Give your team its own identity, watch your tactics come alive on matchday and manage the victories, setbacks and ego clashes that follow.

Offside Deal is a tactical football management game about the decisions that shape a team.

Choose your formation, assign player roles, prepare for the next opponent and decide how you want your side to play. Once the match begins, your plan is put to the test. You can react to events from the touchline, adjust your approach and take on short-term objectives that influence how the game unfolds. You can shape the plan, but your players still have to execute it.

Build a Team That Fits Together

The best eleven players do not always make the best team.

Every player brings different attributes, preferred roles, form and personality. A great finisher still needs someone to create the chance. A talented midfielder can struggle in the wrong position. An ordinary player might become essential because they fit perfectly into your system.

Squad chemistry matters too. Strong relationships can help players get the best out of each other when it counts, while tension between teammates can make important moments less reliable.

You need to decide whether to build around your best individuals or create a team that works as a unit.

Find Your Way to Play

Your team's identity is shaped by two connected layers.

The first is your formation and the roles you assign. This determines your team's structure and the positions where your players operate.

The second is your collection of tactical styles. These styles determine how your team approaches particular situations. You might defend deep, attack through midfield, target a powerful finisher or commit more players forward when chasing a result.

Tactical styles are not simple passive bonuses. They let you turn the strengths of your squad into a match plan. A strong Target Man can become the focal point of a direct attacking system. With a group of players with high physical attributes you may create a high-pressing machine, while disciplined defenders and holding midfielders can give you the foundation for absorbing pressure and striking on the counter.

This connects squad building directly to deck building. Signing a new player can open up a completely different tactical direction, while finding a powerful style may change the kind of player you want to recruit. Choose styles that suit your squad, combine effects that support the same plan and build a system your players can bring to life.

Make Decisions from the Touchline

A good plan will not survive every match unchanged.

You can switch mentality, make substitutions and respond to situations that you encounter during matches. Manager decisions may offer an immediate benefit, set an objective for the next few events or force you to choose between two imperfect options.

Do you keep trusting the system? Do you protect a lead? Do you replace your best but tired finisher or leave him on the pitch in case he delivers a last minute tap-in?

Sometimes the right decision works. Sometimes football has other ideas.

Manage More Than the Match

Results follow your players back into the dressing room.

Morale can rise and fall. Egos can grow after strong performances. Loyalty can be tested, relationships can deteriorate and rivalries can become personal. Players may come to you with problems that cannot be solved by changing the formation.

You will not keep everyone happy. Supporting one player may frustrate another and avoiding a difficult conversation may escalate the problem.

Improve the Club Between Fixtures

Between fixtures, decide where your budget is needed most. Invest in club facilities, sign players discovered through scout reports and packs or improve your existing squad through training. When ordinary preparation is not enough, you may also turn to more drastic ways of gaining an advantage.

Meet Expectations

The board sets expectations at the beginning of each season and gives you an additional objective to pursue. Results, league position and your progress towards those goals affect their confidence in you.

Sponsors offer more ways to earn money through match objectives and longer commitments. Their rewards can help transform the club, but only if you deliver what you promised.

Fight for promotion, avoid relegation and try to build something that can survive across multiple seasons. If the results do not go your way and the board loses faith, your time at the club may come to an early end.

Find Your Own Way to Success

Football rarely offers one correct answer. What works with one squad may be completely wrong for another.

Success comes from recognising what your players can do, building around their strengths and adapting when circumstances change. There is no perfect system, only one that works for your squad, your next opponent and the moment you find yourself in.

Features

  • Build and manage a squad with its own tactical identity

  • Choose formations, player roles, lineups and match mentality

  • Experience event-driven matches focused on decisive moments

  • Combine tactical styles that react to players and match situations

  • Make substitutions and manager decisions during matches

  • Manage player form, stamina, chemistry, morale, loyalty and ego

  • Deal with personalities, relationships, rivalries and club events

  • Improve your squad through training, transfers and reward packs

  • Work towards sponsor objectives and board expectations

  • Chase promotion, fight relegation and build across multiple seasons

A fortune is built in one lifetime. A dynasty across generations.

No fixed end. As long as you have an heir, you play on as the next generation, with what you left behind and the taxes that came with it.

Old Money is an elegant economic life sim: you start at 18 with almost empty pockets – and decide, month by month, how a first paycheck becomes an empire. And how much of it your heirs will carry on.

💼 Build your empire – across every asset class

  • Run companies: staff, marketing, quality, five pricing strategies, research, holding supply chains and IPOs. Every company has its own market position, and competitors attack it month after month.
  • Stocks & crypto: realistic prices, dividends, percentage trading – and yes: stocks and coins can crash completely.
  • Real estate: buy, renovate, upgrade, develop plots – with tenants who have profiles of their own.
  • Politics: build social influence and climb the ladder – from city council all the way to the top.
  • Underworld: fast money in the shadows. But the heat rises – get caught and you lose part of your wealth and spend up to 24 months in jail.

🏆 Fight for the top spot

Rival moguls are not set dressing: they snatch acquisition targets from under you and drive prices up in bidding wars. In return, you can launch hostile takeovers of smaller rivals and swallow their empires. The national rich list is a real race.

👑 Family, inheritance, dynasty

Your partner has a career and wealth of their own. Your children are born with traits and talents and can later join the family business. You retire at 65; by 80 at the latest, your life ends – then the next generation inherits money, real estate and luxury goods, and you play on as your child. In the end, the dynasty grade (F to S) sums up your life's work in a single mark.

🎲 Every decision carries weight

Economic cycles, progressive taxes and inflation. Events with real choices instead of pure randomness. Insurance, health, your credit rating at the bank – and the yearly OLD MONEY GAZETTE, whose outlook genuinely moves next year's market.

♾️ Built to keep you playing

  • Permanent meta progression: achievements unlock starting bonuses and new scenarios – across all save games
  • Prestige mode: start the endless dynasty in a harsher world
  • 4 starting scenarios, 3 difficulty levels, 3 save slots, rare once-in-a-century opportunities

Fully localized in English, German, Spanish, French, Brazilian Portuguese, Polish and Russian.

Early Access: the game is fully playable. During Early Access we refine balancing and content together with the community – the price will increase at the full 1.0 release.

《On the Hook》 is a single-player roguelike that blends prediction, betting, and ability-building mechanics, featuring a pixel-art aesthetic and a "black-and-gold" casino visual style. You play as a gambler deep in debt to the house, struggling to survive across the floors of an ever-expanding casino. You must endure 18 consecutive nights and earn enough money to cover the repayment amounts, which increase with each passing night.

Every night, the casino sees the emergence of one "hottest" high-roller table and one "coldest" shark table.

There are no fixed figures displayed at the tables themselves; the players' stakes remain concealed at the table corners, and a single hidden wager can simultaneously impact multiple tables. You must expend limited investigation action points to count cards, make deductions, activate your "third eye," or even secretly rig the game, using interconnected information to pinpoint which tables are "hot" or "cold."

Bet on a "whale" table, and you’ll walk away with a quick payout from the winner—cash you can use immediately. Bet on a "shark" table, and you’ll lend money to a gambler blinded by the urge to recoup losses, securing an IOU that grows night by night.

After the nightly settlement, you can take your remaining chips to the black market to purchase permanent ability cards and marked cards. Whether it’s boosting card-counting efficiency, raising your betting stakes, running a loan shark operation, diversifying investments, going all-in early, or directly altering the numbers on the table—every purchase shapes a unique money-making engine for the round!

You have a kanban board, a team, a budget, and a deadline. The client wants it On Time,

In Full. How you get there is up to you.

BUILD YOUR TEAM

Hire junior and senior developers, QA engineers, and project managers — each with their

tasks. A senior costs three times as much but rarely fails.

OTIF puts you in the chair of a delivery-obsessed project manager.

You have a kanban board, a team, a budget, and a deadline. The client wants it On Time,

In Full. How you get there is up to you.

BUILD YOUR TEAM

Hire junior and senior developers, QA engineers, and project managers. Each has their

own day rate, skill ceiling, and success rate. A junior dev is cheap but risky on large

tasks. A senior costs three times as much but rarely fails.

MANAGE YOUR BACKLOG

Every feature starts as a card. Move it from Backlog → To Do → In Progress → Testing →

A relaxing and immersive experience where you will camp, fish, and forage to survive as you make your way along a pixel art coastline, following in the footsteps of the traditional Australian swagman.

A "swagman" is a term for a nomadic person who would typically travel with minimal gear consisting mostly of their swag (a bedroll) and a few other items.

You will face a realistic simulated coastal bush environment, be immersed among sounds captured authentically in the Australian bush, and discover what lies at the end of your journey.

The environments in this game have all been hand pixeled and all of the sounds you will hear in this game - from the weather, to footsteps, to the laugh of a kookaburra, to the gentle trickle of a stream or the lapping of waves - were captured live in the Australian bush by the developer in an attempt to provide an experience that feels authentically Australian and connected to nature.

Fishing and Foraging

There are many ways to go about surviving in Once Upon a Swagman, but at the heart of it all are the foraging and fishing systems.

Some swaggies may find they prefer sticking to the bush and living off of what bush tucker they can forage there. Others may prefer to take to the ocean to catch fish and explore reefs.

But perhaps the most successful swaggies will find a harmonious balance between both of these aspects. Instead of eating your small foraged items, use them as bait to catch bigger fish, and then use those fish to catch even bigger fish!

Or... use your fish as bait on land to lure out a meal of crabs... just make sure the seagulls don't fly off with your fish!

Fire making

A camp does not feel like home until the camp fire is lit... but you're going to have to work for it. If you want to cook your fish you're going to have to build up your fire first. You'll have to find suitable dry tinder to start a fire, and supply it with enough smaller and larger fuel to really get it going.

But... be careful. On hot and dry days you might find your fire spreads a little further than you intended.

They call Australia the land of droughts and flooding rains. If it's not one extreme it's the other. Just as you might find yourself amidst a catastrophic bushfire, on a wet and rainy day you might find yourself unable to find material dry enough to get a fire started at all as you shiver cold and alone with no fish to eat.

A little preparation goes a long way: keep a few bits of dry tinder handy, set up a tarp shelter to keep the rain off your fire wood, and you'll have a cozy camp where you can listen to the pitter patter of the rain on the tarp as you eat your hard earned fish.

Unlock New Skills

The seasoned swaggie has a larger toolkit. As you complete survival tasks you will unlock new tools to help you survive as the terrain becomes harsher and resources more scarce. Once you are fully kitted out you will be able to use all of these tools:

  • Knife

  • Fishing Rod

  • Shovel

  • Spear

  • Axe

  • Raft

  • Sling

You will also gain skill points as you level up which you can invest into attributes in a skill tree that best suit the way you want to survive in the bush.

Lucky Finds!

It's the lucky country, or so they say, and there are various ways you can snag your own lucky finds. You can fish for, dig for, or simply stumble upon various treasures that will aid you in your journey.

Every legend has a beginning. This one has quite a few revisions.

A bard decides to become the hero of his own ballad. In his imagination, stoves are volcanoes and tables are cliffs. Dying after falling off a ladle? An unacceptable ending.

One Bard Move is a 3D precision platformer packed with oversized obstacles, demanding jumps and decidedly unheroic deaths.

Grand adventures, tiny footholds

In One Last Draw, step into a deadly game of Bomb Cards. Build your deck with Bomb Cards lurking within it, and keep drawing to rack up points and advance to the next round.

Draw one more card. Watch your score soar—or lose it all.

The rules are simple: every time you HIT, your score increases, but you might draw a Bomb Card and lose everything. Will you risk one more draw, or STAND while you're ahead?The choice is yours.

Don’t Lose It All

Once your health drops to zero, all points earned in this round vanish completely! You can only clear the stage by wisely choosing to draw more cards or stop in time.

Craft Your Unique Build

Buy cards, chips and permanent upgrades in the shop or through phone‑call events, and pick from available phone‑call choices. Will you feed your greed by embracing greater risks, or outsmart randomness with a steady, safe playstyle? Your build decides everything.

One More Claw is a 3D physics claw machine with roguelike building on the cabinet. The claw grabs by physics. Prizes crowd, slip, and block. A catch only counts when it goes into the chute: confetti, a short camera shake, then inspect. A miss refunds that drop. There is no penalty.

Round score is base times multiplier. When you hit the target, the scoreboard blows out (BLASTED) and the round clears. You do not have to spend every drop. Catching is feel; blasting the target is the build.

The claw

  • Aim, drop, close, lift, deliver. It counts only if it enters the chute.

  • After a catch, keep or discard. Keep puts it on the shelf for this round's combo. Discard gives a fixed score. Glass shatters on discard and still adds score.

  • The shelf has limited slots. A full shelf banks that rack and clears, then you keep grabbing.

  • Drops per round are limited. A miss refunds the drop.

Blasting the target

Clear the round by reaching the target score. After a blast you pick one of three offers, then the next round. Mini-bosses and the boss raise the target and grant extra drops. Normal mode ends when you beat the boss. Endless mode keeps your progress and keeps raising the target.

Roguelike building

Prizes have tags, and tags can stack. Scoring reads the tags on the shelf. The cabinet holds plush, glass, tin, huge pieces, rares, and more. One prize can wear several tags.

  • Plush: each adds base. Metal: more base, and one on the shelf also adds multiplier. Huge: each adds a lot of base.

  • Glass: adds multiplier. On discard it shatters and adds extra score.

  • Cat: exactly one adds high multiplier; two or more cancel it. A fish on the shelf also gives the cat base.

  • Fish: every two add multiplier. Glass on the shelf gives each fish base.

  • Rabbit: keeping one banks base that survives a full shelf; each on the shelf also adds base.

  • Rare: one on the shelf is enough to add multiplier.

The three-offer after a clear can add prizes to the pile, add a tag type, or upgrade a tag. The shop sells figurines that change the run (extra drops, miss refund, clear gold, shop discount, and so on).

Characters and growth trees

Meta progression is unique characters, each with their own growth tree. Different characters take different upgrade paths, and that changes how a run starts and how it plays.

Look and controls

Slightly retro, refined cartoon: simple shapes, readable plush, glass, tin, and plastic. Keyboard and mouse, or gamepad. Thirteen languages.

The demons took Black Raven Valley. The gold is still there. So every night, one stubborn gunslinger walks through the portal — kills until the valley is knee-deep in coin, and then faces the only decision that matters: leave rich, or stay for one more volley.

Extract or die trying.

Survive escalating waves of demons across a hand-built valley — abandoned villages, flooded graveyards, a dead forest that watches back. Gold you carry is gold you can lose: walk out through the portal and bank all of it, or die and keep a salvaged cut. The portal is always the safe choice. The next wave is always the richer one.

The build is the game.

You move. Your arsenal fires on its own. Every level-up deals a hand of cards — new guns, upgrades, and trinkets of debatable value. Max a gun, max its paired artifact, and it evolves into something the demons file complaints about.

Features:

  • A hand-crafted valley, not a random soup — every road, graveyard, and ruin placed on purpose; only the run itself is unpredictable

  • Eight gun classes — from a crowd-shoving blunderbuss to a lightning turret with opinions

  • Weapon evolutions — pair the right gun with the right relic and reforge it mid-run

  • Artifacts of pathetic power — cursed trinkets, questionable sausages, a famous liar's glass eye; the world is grim, the treasures are embarrassing

  • The extraction decision — bank everything at the portal or gamble the haul on one more wave

  • Meta progression — spend banked gold in the village between raids; death pays, just poorly

  • Bosses with manners — every deadly thing telegraphs before it kills you

  • Short runs, long consequences — ~20 minutes a raid, benchmark auto-tuning, and a valley that remembers being paid

One Second Is Fast. You're Faster.

In a fleeting second, observe your surroundings and spot opportunities you'd normally never have time to notice.

Use Everything Around You

Objects and mechanisms in the environment can all be part of the solution. Observe, interact, and turn the situation around.

Change What's Already in Motion

Catch objects in midair, change their position and direction, and alter what happens next.

Solve It Your Way

Use your abilities, the environment, or even your enemies' weapons. Find your own solution before the second is over.

A hyper-realistic K-office drama.

This is a story about quitting, and a record of your final attitude on the job.

In your last week, will you leave behind "work" or "people"?

Will you fill out every handoff document to be remembered as a flawless senior? Or will you throw all your tasks out the window, hoard office snacks, and completely lose it?

The game doesn't judge your morality. It simply shows you the unvarnished consequences of the attitude you chose.

It's okay to mess up. After all... you're leaving this company anyway.

Experience a final 5 days where alienation and absolute freedom coexist.

Key Gameplay

  • 5-Day Schedule Management System

    • Plan and manage your daily activities during your final 5 days before resignation.

  • Dialogue Choices & Player Actions

    • Chat with coworkers to promise future catch-ups, or focus on handing over your tasks for those left behind.

    • You can even do nothing to kill time, or vent your long-pent-up feelings toward the company and colleagues with sharp, stinging remarks and satisfyingly unpredictable antics.

  • Multiple Endings Driven by Your Choices (4 Endings Total)

    • Every choice and conversation directly shapes not only the protagonist's attitude, but also how colleagues perceive and react to them.

    • Through 3 main endings and 1 hidden ending, experience the final farewell defined entirely by your choices.

Game Features

  • Realistic K-Office Life: Encounter all-too-familiar office personalities—from sociopathic team leads and out-of-touch seniors to unbothered rookies. Experience the frustrating, absurd realities of office life through painfully relatable dialogue every employee knows too well.

  • High Freedom of Choice: No moral right or wrong. Face only the direct results of the attitude you choose to take.

  • A Thought-Provoking Story: Through the narrative of your final five days, go beyond simply asking "How will others remember me?" and reflect on a deeper question: "How do I want to remember my own final moments?"

A Game With Challenging, Innovative Gameplay

Can you tell when the machine is making things up?

Build your vocabulary, outwit an AI, and test your linguistic skills in this word game. Every round is a new mental workout—build, decode, and define your way to victory with hand-crafted visuals scanned from in-house made physical assets.

Four Modes of Play

  • Tile-Build Rounds

    • Like other word games, but with less limits: you’re given as many tiles of a letter set as you want—and one “blank” tile you can reuse as any single letter infinite times. Your goal: find five words that use the rarest letters the most before time runs out

  • Definition Rounds

    • Put your knowledge of English to the test. In this round, you choose between one real definition and three AI-generated definitions. Spot the truth; do you know better than the AI?

    • Every round you get a unique set of definitions. The AI tends to have patterns, though, so the right answer will often stand out

  • Most-Common Rounds

    • Build the most common words you can with the tiles you have available

  • Define Rounds

    • Put your summarization and writing skills to the test by defining one of the words you've made

Why You’ll Love It

  • Hand-Built, Authentic Art: Every asset in the game—tiles, backgrounds, UI elements—is either 3D-scanned from real-world objects or hand-drawn.
